## About the trip

The first few days take you through mainland Ecuador. In Quito, you’ll walk through the historic centre and visit the equator. In Cotopaxi, you’ll see the high-altitude national park and Limpiopungo Lake. Then the route takes you through Quilotoa and Baños, with a crater lake, waterfalls, a canyon and the famous Swing at the End of the World.

After the Andes, you’ll spend three days in the Mashpi Reserve. Activities vary according to the weather, group size and guests’ fitness levels. The stay generally includes cloud forest walks, wildlife watching, early morning activities and evening outings.

In the Galápagos, the itinerary takes you out on the water. You’ll start on Santa Cruz, with its giant tortoises and lava tunnels, then visit Bartolomé and either North Seymour or South Plaza. From there, you’ll continue to Isabela for the wetlands, Las Tintoreras, Sierra Negra Volcano and Concha Perla Bay.

## What stands out

Each region of Ecuador brings a change of scenery. The first few days are in the Andes: Quito sits at 2,800 m, the Cotopaxi excursion reaches about 3,800 m, and Quilotoa is at roughly 3,900 m. From the cool highlands, you’ll descend to the milder climate of Baños, then move on to the cloud forest at Mashpi.

You’ll spend three days in the Mashpi Reserve, which covers about 1,300 hectares, staying at the lodge on a full-board basis. Early morning walks in the forest may be available, the main nature activities take place during the day, and night walks may be arranged after dinner when conditions allow. The stay gives you time to see the forest at different times of day.

The six-day Galápagos leg brings another change of scenery from island to island. On Santa Cruz, the focus is on giant tortoises, the highlands and lava tunnels. Bartolomé shows you the archipelago’s volcanic landscapes and offers a chance to snorkel off the shore. North Seymour is known for birds and sea lions, while South Plaza offers a walk past cliffs and sesuvium plants. On Isabela, you’ll see mangroves, lagoons, Las Tintoreras, the Sierra Negra crater and Concha Perla Bay.

The trip combines upscale city hotels and nature lodges. Your accommodation includes a Royal Suite at the 5-star Plaza Grande in Quito, the 4-star La Cienega in the Cotopaxi area, the 5-star Samari in Baños, Mashpi Lodge, an ocean-view stay at the 4-star Solymar on Santa Cruz, and an Ocean View Room at the 4-star Iguana Crossing on Isabela. You’ll have a comfortable base along the way, including where the focus is on nature and active excursions. Some evenings after transfers are left free, giving you time to rest before boat trips and early departures on the islands.
